title: The behavior of red foxes
body: Red foxes are solitary hunters, most active at dawn and dusk. A red fox uses its bushy tail for balance and warmth, and its orange fur blends into autumn forest light. This article explores how foxes cache food, raise kits in dens, and adapt to farmland and cities alike.

title: Vulpes vulpes: the adaptable red fox
body: Vulpes vulpes is the most widely distributed wild land carnivore on Earth. Despite the Latin name, this is the same red fox familiar from folklore. We look at its range, diet of rodents and berries, and why this fox species thrives near humans.

title: Foxes in folklore and culture
body: From Aesop to Japanese kitsune, the fox has played the trickster for millennia. The red fox in particular appears across European and East Asian storytelling as a symbol of cunning. What makes this animal so compelling to human imagination?

title: How gray wolves hunt in packs
body: The gray wolf is a cooperative apex predator. A wolf pack coordinates to test, chase, and exhaust prey much larger than any single wolf could handle. We examine pack hierarchy, territorial howling, and hunting strategy in Canis lupus.

title: Why wolves howl at the moon
body: Wolves do not actually howl at the moon — but howling is central to wolf life. A gray wolf howls to rally the pack, defend territory, and locate separated members across kilometers of forest. The science behind the sound.

title: Training your new dog: the first week
body: Bringing home a dog is joyful and chaotic. The first week sets the tone: crate training, house rules, and short positive sessions. Whether a puppy or a rescue, a domestic dog learns fastest with consistency and patience.

title: The search-and-rescue dogs of the mountains
body: Avalanche rescue dogs can locate a buried person faster than a team of humans with probes. We follow a search-and-rescue dog unit through winter training in the Alps and meet the handlers behind these remarkable working dogs.

title: Brown bears and the art of hibernation
body: A brown bear can spend seven months in its den without eating, drinking, or urinating. Before winter, bears enter hyperphagia, consuming up to 20,000 calories a day. Inside the physiology of Ursus arctos and its long sleep.

title: A hiker's guide to bear safety
body: Most bear encounters end peacefully when hikers follow simple rules: make noise, store food properly, and never run. Knowing whether you face a curious brown bear or a defensive mother changes how you should respond.

title: Deer migration through the seasons
body: Each year, deer herds move between summer alpine meadows and sheltered winter valleys. Red deer and their relatives time these journeys to snow depth and forage. Tracking collars reveal how precisely deer remember ancestral routes.

title: Coral reefs: the underwater cities
body: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor yet host a quarter of all marine species. Parrotfish, clownfish, and countless invertebrates build these living structures — now threatened by warming seas. No land animals appear in this article.

title: Baking sourdough bread at home
body: A sourdough starter needs only flour, water, and time. This guide covers feeding schedules, folding techniques, and how to read your dough. From first bubbly levain to a crackling crust fresh from the oven.

title: Chasing the northern lights
body: The aurora borealis appears when solar wind particles excite gases high in the atmosphere. We explain KP indexes, the best latitudes, and how to photograph the green curtains of the polar night sky.
